name: Peter Whitmer Sr.
role: Fayette farmer whose home hosted the Church’s founding
dateNote: Translation was finished at his home in June 1829, and the Church was organized there on 6 April 1830.
importance: Peter Whitmer Sr. owned the farm in Fayette, New York, where Joseph Smith finished translating in June 1829. The Church was organized at his home on 6 April 1830, and several early revelations were received there. Section 128 recalls “the voice of God in the chamber of old Father Whitmer.” He moved to Ohio and Missouri, became disaffected, and died in Richmond, Missouri.
connections: He was the father of David, John, Christian, and Peter Whitmer Jr., and of Elizabeth Ann, who married Oliver Cowdery. His wife was Mary Musselman.

sources.title: Peter Whitmer Sr., Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: Dates and events checked on JSP; death 13 Aug. 1854 read from a cut fragment. JSP does not list his children; they are given from the David Whitmer and Oliver Cowdery JSP pages and general knowledge.
